FROMGIT: pinctrl: mediatek: Add pm_ops to pinctrl-paris pinctrl variants that include pinctrl-paris.h (and not pinctrl-mtk-common.h) also need to use pm_ops to setup wake mask properly, so copy over the pm_ops from common to paris variant. CRAS: hfp_ag - Handle the case hfp_ag starts twice Bluetooth stack notifices CRAS about remove device's capability and there's a chance that it uses more than one events to let CRAS know the whole capability of remote headset. BlueZ sends dbus messages to CRAS to notify remove device's state and capability. There's a chance that it uses more than one message to communicate whole capability. If the 1st message from BlueZ doesn't include all audio profiles the headset supports, CRAS need to handle headset capability update in the later message and that could trigger cras_hfp_ag_start be called twice. This change fixes a memory leak in cras_hfp_ag_start, before the fix when paired and then disconnect specific BT headset. It'll stay as audio I/O option forever. BUG=chromium:968934 TEST=Use LG HBS700 to pair, and then disconnect it from BT settings UI. Verify that audio settings doesn't show LG HBS700 as option. Test fresh pair multiple times as there's a chance to reproduce it. CRAS: bt_device - Fix the logic to start conn watch flow The BT connect watch callback regularly checks if each of the supported profiles are connected, and decide when to expose A2DP/HFP node to audio settings. Existing logic in CRAS restarts this connection watch flow if bluetoothd tells CRAS the device capability changes. However often the capability change is unrelated to A2DP or HFP so we can skip it. sys_power: update /run/autotest_pause_ethernet_hook mtime We're going to modify check_ethernet.hook so that it doesn't keep removing the lock file for us. But it also likes to do staleness / hung-task computations using the modification time, so we should actually 'touch' the file (open(..., 'w+')), instead of just appending. It's also nice to update our lock each time we need it, rather than grabbing it only once for the entire duration of the script. Finally, drop some of the "fd" integer comparisons, as open() returns file objects, not integers. BUG=chromium:966965 TEST=power_SuspendStress Change-Id: I38dc3abf79ef3231ce7cc2d232d909ff8158d4f3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1637852 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org>

check_ethernet: hold /run/autotest_pause_ethernet_hook for script duration Locks aren't sufficient if only one side actually acquires them. Let's acquire the lock for the duration of the script. We also shouldn't be removing the lock file unless we really think it's held by a hung task. Test jobs can handle updating the file modification time. Also, update /var/lock to /run/lock. /run/lock is bind-mounted to /var/lock, so these are the same, but it's nice to use the same path name. See also https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/473968. Quirky shell note: POSIX only specifies fd redirection for single-digit numbers, so '9' is the highest number I can use for 'exec 9>>${FOO}'. This would be a little nicer if I could use bash... BUG=chromium:966965 TEST=power_SuspendStress, see check_ethernet abort TEST=manual, don't find check_ethernet running 'ping' tests, etc., while we hold the lock: `while :; do touch /run/autotest_pause_ethernet_hook flock /run/autotest_pause_ethernet_hook pgrep -l ping sleep 1 done` Cq-Depend: chromium:1637852 Change-Id: I07274519a72fb47fc5d64038649586c7d2b6a819 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1637489 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org>

FIXUP: CHROMIUM: platform/chrome: wilco_ec: Add charge scheduling backend There were several mistakes in the initial implementation: The EC property IDs were all messed up in the initial commit. This corrects them to follow the specification at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lNgipPdQJySZ8VIPtM0UO0SGeupBR7Vbdu-obFmZ8mI The EC interface specification was incorrect in the format for the Advanced Charging arguments: http://issuetracker.google.com/133749406 This fixes the format. Servod: Added handling of additional IPC signals for proper shutdown Servod requires a shutdown sequence to be executed for it to cleanly stop in a known good configuration. If the process terminates in a way which is not handled then servod may not be able to resume until the appropriate recovery path is taken. This recovery path may require involve the host system having resources locked resulting in 'Resource Busy' errors. External programs which communicate with the servod process can stall when timeouts are missing. If the Servo or the DUT is busy responding to commands, it may not be in a state which permits it to respond properly to the unexpected initialization sequence so physically disconnecting and power cycling components may be needed as recovery. This does not fully resolve that situation but seems to reduce the rate of occurrence. BRANCH=servo BUG=b:134093234 TEST=Verified servod and servo recovers reliably from a variety of shutdown conditions including closing terminal and sending various classes of keyboard signals including SIGINT, SIGTSTP, and SIGQUIT Signed-off-by: Brian Nemec <bnemec@chromium.org> Change-Id: I6950365caa799a95698fb37083f92ef5da095cf2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1636862 Commit-Ready: Brian Nemec <bnemec@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Nemec <bnemec@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>
